ballot: All 435 seats in the U.S. House of Representatives.
35 of 100 U.S. Senate seats: 33 regular seats plus special elections in Florida and Ohio to fill the seats vacated by Marco Rubio and JD Vance. Republicans are defending 22 of them and Democrats 13.
36 governorships, plus state legislatures, ballot measures and local offices.
control: Republicans hold the Senate 53-47 (45 Democrats and 2 independents who caucus with them) and a majority in the House.

dates.text: Election Day. The first polls close at 6 p.m. ET in parts of Indiana and Kentucky; the last close in Hawaii and Alaska.
The new Congress is sworn in.
